title: Sarcopenia Diagnostic using spectral CT
summary:
Fatty liver and muscle wasting have a negative influence on the clinical course of cancer patients. In this study, a new technique for fat quantification in the liver and skeletal muscles using spectral CT will be validated in patients with gastrointestinal tumors under systematic therapy by MRI measurements.

Furthermore, the suitability of spectral CT fat values to detect fatty liver (hepatic steatosis) and muscle wasting (sarcopenia) will be examined using established radiological methods (single-energy CT), and clinical measurements (e.g. hand strength). Further, the relationship between spectral CT liver and muscle fat values ​ and the clinical outcome (e.g. survival, quality of life) will be evaluated.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Overlapping lesion of colon

interventions.name: Gastrointestinal cancer patients under systematic therapy with (spectral)-CT scans for clinical indications and additional MRI exams, clinical muscle and functional tests, and questionnaires on exercise and nutritional behavior for study purposes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Patients with gastrointestinal cancer entities under palliative or adjuvant chemotherapy
2) Clinical indication for a CT scan
3) CT scan in the spectral-CT
Exclusion criteria:
1) Presence of other independent risk factors for sarcopenia (e.g. neuromuscular diseases, severe dysphagia, malabsorption due to extensive previous abdominal operations, known food intolerances). 
2) Surgery with immobilization during the study period
3) MRI contraindications (e.g. foreign materials (pacemaker, staple sutures), claustrophobia)
4) Spondylodesis material at the level of the 3rd lumbar vertebra
